mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate over three consecutive months signals a tightening monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.10) during periods when FEDFUNDS rises for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% indicates weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when GDPC1 YoY change < -2%.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in the unemployment rate above 0.3 percentage points for three consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which reduces consumer spending and corporate margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative during periods of sustained UNRATE increases > 0.3pp for three months.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 0.5% for four consecutive months indicates contraction in manufacturing output, which depresses earnings expectations and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when INDPRO declines > 0.5% for four consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both the federal funds rate and core CPI inflation above their respective 12-month averages signals a dual monetary and inflationary shock, which increases real discount rates and erodes real corporate earnings, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL exceed their 12-month averages simultaneously.

mechanism_narrative: A coordinated decline in both real personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) and housing starts (HOUST) by more than 1% month-over-month indicates a broad-based collapse in demand, which reduces corporate revenue and profit growth, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 and HOUST both fall > 1% MoM
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when both GDPC1 and HOUST decline > 1% MoM.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent rise in payroll employment (PAYEMS) above 0.5% month-over-month for five consecutive months signals a robust labor market expansion, which supports consumer spending and corporate profit margins, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive during periods of sustained PAYEMS growth > 0.5% MoM for five months.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly increase in the industrial production index (INDPRO) above 0.4% for six consecutive months signals a broad-based supply-side expansion, which boosts corporate earnings and supports higher equity valuations, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive during periods of sustained INDPRO growth > 0.4% MoM for six months.
